objective: Perform a fresh-context, read-only five-axis final review of the complete pre-final v0.3 implementation and evidence, reporting every finding with severity and exact evidence.
deliverable: A structured review receipt covering implementation, tests, safety/security, evidence/integrity, and documentation/operability, with an explicit acceptance recommendation.
read_scope: fixtures/adaptive-task-orchestrator-write-dag/ (source, tests, README, named run, and nested Git metadata)
write_scope: Unique automatically cleaned unittest TemporaryDirectory paths outside the project if the reviewer reruns tests

authoritative_facts: The reviewer did not author T1 through T5 and must independently test claims rather than rely on receipts alone.
integrity.sha256, the final validation receipt, and this reviewer's root-saved receipt are intentionally absent until review acceptance.
v0.1 and v0.2 are immutable; the project root is not a Git repository.
user_constraints: Read-only project review; no fixes, dependency installs, network, external runtimes, v0.1/v0.2 mutations, or destructive Git actions.
permissions: Read declared paths and use only automatically cleaned OS temporary directories through existing tests.
non_goals: Do not demand deferred third-party OpenAPI validation, stale-lock recovery, a second topology, cross-host clocks, or production/performance claims as v0.3 acceptance requirements.

acceptance_checks: Implementation axis: atomic materializer ownership/cleanup behavior, validator fail-closed boundaries, and event-transition/overlap logic satisfy the spec and ADRs.
Test axis: meaningful normal, malformed, conflict, failure-injection, cleanup/retry, transition, and overlap cases are exercised and reproducible.
Safety/security axis: path validation, non-overwrite behavior, lock/cleanup ownership, input parsing, command invocation, and write scopes have no Critical or Required defect.
Evidence/integrity axis: receipts and summaries reconcile with files, routes, immutable contracts, manifests, hashes, and the bounded single-host claim.
Documentation/operability axis: README/spec/ADRs clearly describe commands, failure semantics, compatibility, and deferred limitations.
Report severity as Critical, Required, or Advisory; acceptance requires zero Critical and zero Required findings.
